curiosities: Its second cartridge slot plays Game Boy Advance games, run by the same ARM7 processor family as the GBA's.
PictoChat, built into every DS, let nearby consoles swap hand-drawn messages without the internet.
Nintendo said DS stood for both 'Dual Screen' and 'Developers' System'.
Nintendo Wi-Fi Connection, its online service, shut down in May 2014.
It launched in North America on 21 November 2004.
Its lower screen is a touch screen, played with a stylus.
It has two ARM processors: an ARM9 at 67 MHz and an ARM7 at 33 MHz.
Its built-in microphone lets games hear the player, as in Nintendogs.
The DS Lite of 2006 is smaller, with brighter screens.
The DSi of 2008 added two cameras and an SD card slot, and dropped the Game Boy Advance slot.
Brain Age (Brain Training in Europe) brought it many players who had never owned a console.
With over 154 million sold, it is Nintendo's best-selling handheld.
